$comment: VAT and percentage tax parameters. Draft pending research reconciliation.

legalBasis: NIRC Sec 109(CC) & 236(G), as amended by RA 10963 (TRAIN)
RA 11976 (EOPT) & RR 3-2024 — subject to 3-year CPI adjustment
vatThreshold.notes: ₱3,000,000 gross annual sales (post-EOPT: 'gross sales', accrual) — reconfirmed Aug 26, 2026; no adjustment RR has issued. The first EOPT-cycle CPI adjustment falls due around January 2027 — re-check then; the 8% ceiling and percentage-tax boundary ride on it. Don't confuse this with the separate ₱3.6M VAT-exempt ceiling for residential dwellings (Sec 109(P), RR 1-2024) that some guides conflate with it.

legalBasis: NIRC Sec 116, as amended by RA 11534 (CREATE) — 1% from Jul 1 2020 to Jun 30 2023, 3% thereafter
percentageTaxRate.notes: 3% of gross quarterly sales/receipts for non-VAT taxpayers under the threshold, unless the 8% option is elected.

vatRegistrationDeadline.value: Register as VAT taxpayer before the end of the month following the month the ₱3M threshold was exceeded
vatRegistrationDeadline.notes: Once past the threshold you are liable for output VAT whether or not you register on time.

servicesAccrualBasis.value: Since EOPT, VAT and percentage tax on services are computed on gross SALES (billed/accrued), no longer on collections
servicesAccrualBasis.notes: Output VAT on receivables that stay uncollected past the agreed credit term may be deducted from the NEXT quarter's output VAT under the Sec 110(D) conditions (post-Apr 27, 2024 credit sale, written credit term, VAT shown and paid, not claimed as bad debt) — and added back if later collected. Pre-Apr 27, 2024 receivables stay on the collection basis.

vatFilingFrequency.value: Quarterly only — BIR Form 2550Q within 25 days after each taxable quarter; the monthly 2550M is no longer required, though optional monthly filing for the first two months of a quarter remains allowed
legalBasis: NIRC Sec 114(A), as amended by RA 10963 (quarterly from Jan 1, 2023)
RMC 52-2023 (optional 2550M — no deadline, no penalty, no open cases)
vatFilingFrequency.notes: Under EOPT (RR 4-2024) returns may be filed and taxes paid anywhere — electronically or at any AAB/RDO — and the old 25% wrong-venue surcharge is gone.

digitalServicesVat.value: 12% VAT applies to digital services consumed in the Philippines, including those of nonresident providers — and for B2B purchases the Philippine business must withhold and remit the VAT itself (reverse charge) via BIR Form 1600-VT
digitalServicesVat.notes: Hits any business buying ads, SaaS, cloud hosting, or marketplace services from nonresident platforms: withhold 12%, remit on Form 1600-VT by the 10th of the following month, and (if VAT-registered) claim it back as input VAT supported by the 1600-VT. Nonresident providers handle B2C sales themselves via the VDS portal (Form 2550-DS). Local digital sellers stay under the ordinary VAT/percentage-tax rules and the ₱3M threshold.

legalBasis: NIRC Sec 237, as amended by RA 11976 (EOPT)
invoiceIssuanceThreshold.notes: An invoice must issue for every sale of ₱500 or more; VAT-registered sellers issue one regardless of amount, and any seller must on the buyer's request. Non-VAT sellers may issue one aggregated end-of-day invoice for the day's sub-₱500 sales. Adjusted for CPI every 3 years from EOPT effectivity — first adjustment expected ~Jan 2027 alongside the ₱3M threshold review.
